44: S3 encrypts buckets and server-side encrypts objects by default with SSE-S3 keys.
45: Storage Gateway encrypts data transfers to AWS storage with SSL by default.

54: Storage Gateways connect on-premises systems with cloud storage.

55: File Gateway caches recent data and connects applications to S3.

56: Volume Gateway provides block storage; cached volumes give low-latency access.

64: Simple routing directs a domain to one resource, such as a website server.
67: Latency routing sends users to the AWS Region with the lowest latency.
68: Multivalue routing returns up to eight healthy records in DNS responses.
90: Reserved Instances can discount on-demand usage by up to 72%.

92: EBS volumes are network drives attached to one EC2 instance at a time.
They are tied to an AZ and persist after instance termination.
Snapshots back up volumes and can move them across AZs.
96: Instance Store is a high-performance disk attached to an EC2 instance.
Its data is lost when the instance stops or terminates.
97: EFS is a regional network file system for hundreds of instances across AZs.
102: Elasticity scales resources up or down to match actual needs.
104: Horizontal scaling adds or removes instances to change their number.
106: ELBs distribute traffic across backend EC2 instances and support health checks.
111: ASGs are free and scale capacity with demand across multiple AZs.

112: S3 bucket names are globally unique, and each bucket belongs to a Region.
122: S3 replication requires versioning on source and destination buckets.
Copies are asynchronous and can be cross-Region or same-Region.
123: Cross-Region Replication copies bucket contents across Regions.
It supports compliance, lower latency, and operational efficiency.
124: Same-Region Replication copies bucket contents within a Region.
Use it to aggregate logs, replicate accounts, or meet data-residency rules.
125: RDS is a managed relational database service queried with SQL.
Supported engines include PostgreSQL, MySQL, Oracle, MariaDB, and SQL Server.
126: Aurora is AWS's cloud-optimized implementation of PostgreSQL or MySQL.
129: DynamoDB is a serverless NoSQL database replicated across three AZs.
131: DynamoDB Global Tables make a table available in multiple Regions.
Active-active replication allows reads and writes in any participating Region.
132: ElastiCache provides managed Redis or Memcached in-memory databases.
136: QuickSight is a serverless, ML-powered business intelligence dashboard service.
142: DMS supports homogeneous and heterogeneous database migrations.

149: Lambda runs functions on demand as serverless FaaS.

150: CloudFormation defines AWS infrastructure as code across most resources.
Reuse templates across Regions and accounts.
151: Elastic Beanstalk is a PaaS for selected languages or Docker.

165: EventBridge reacts to AWS events and schedules processes.

166: CloudTrail audits account activity by recording API calls.

168: X-Ray traces requests across distributed applications in real time.
172: A VPC is a logically isolated network spanning all AZs in a Region.
Create subnets, choose IP ranges, and configure routes and gateways.
A VPC alone cannot connect an on-premises network to the cloud.
176: VPC endpoints privately connect a VPC to AWS services.
The two types are gateway endpoints and interface endpoints.
177: Gateway endpoints support S3 and DynamoDB only.
Add the endpoint as a route-table target for that service's traffic.
178: Interface endpoints support AWS services, including S3.
They use an elastic network interface with a private subnet IP.
The interface is an entry point to the supported service.
181: A subnet is a VPC network partition tied to one Availability Zone.
183: NACLs are stateless subnet-level rules for inbound and outbound traffic.
They use IP addresses and support both DENY and ALLOW rules.
184: Security groups are stateful and apply at EC2 instance or ENI level.
